title: Relative tensor-pullback homology comparison
statement: Let f:X -> S be a morphism of schemes, with the fixed derived categories [def-pc-derived-category], derived pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback], and derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Let E be in D(O_X), K a complex of O_X-modules, and eK:Q(K) ≅ E. Put R=f-inverse O_S and restrict K along the tensor-pullback ring map [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let P be an R-module complex, K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], with a quasi-isomorphism q:P -> K restricted to R. For every O_S-module F, with inverse image [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module], and every integer i, the underlying abelian sheaf of H^i(E tensor^L Lf*(F[0])) is isomorphic to the underlying abelian sheaf of H^i(Tot(P tensor_R f-inverse F[0])) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. No finite Tor amplitude, boundedness, quasi-coherence, coherence or geometric assumption is imposed.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma 20.27.4, Tag 08DE; Tag 08EV, second displayed equality

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions A -> K and L -> F[0]. Exact restriction preserves the first quasi-isomorphism; exact inverse image gives a K-flat complex inverse-image L.

Tensor the zigzag A restricted -> K restricted <- P with inverse-image L. Tensor-cone isomorphisms and K-flatness give quasi-isomorphisms for both arrows. Symmetry and the tensor-cone identity show P tensor inverse-image(L -> F[0]) is a quasi-isomorphism.

Apply the K-flat representative comparison to A,L. Transport derived homology using Q(A -> K), eK, and Q(L -> F[0]). Compose with the three homology isomorphisms of the tensor zigzag and with inverse image commuting with the single complex functor.
